The file lacks a signed completion record, a return-visit or completion entry, and supporting authorization or attendance evidence for the reported actuator replacement. The tenant did not know whether it was replaced and had not seen a contractor since the 5 February visit.

The invoice records have overlapping work descriptions and no stated credit, cancellation, or supersession. Invoice B claims actuator replacement completed on 5 February, while the £372 estimate requesting authorization was sent after the stated service date and the 7 February exchange still had parts and estimate details outstanding. Whether either record supersedes the other, whether both amounts are payable, and how the overlap is treated remain unresolved.

The file note says the landlord's written authority covered diagnosis only and that no written authorization for actuator replacement is in the file. The requested authorization or attendance evidence for actuator work has not been supplied.
The invoice descriptions do not establish whether the £138 diagnostic charge is credited against the £372 record; neither record states whether the other is credited, cancelled, or superseded.
It remains unclear whether the invoice entries represent separate chargeable work or whether one record replaces the other; the records' payment status is also not established.
The source reports no recorded authorization for actuator work, and the tenant has not confirmed whether the actuator was replaced; authorization and completion remain unestablished.
